label: Transgressive Records / Canvasback
release_notes: Third album from Burlington, Vermont singer-songwriter Greg Freeman, after I Looked Out (July 2022) and Burnover (Aug. 2025). Transgressive says Burnover made The New York Times' best albums of 2025 and earned Pitchfork's Best New Album tag.

13 tracks, about 67 minutes, spread over four sides of a double LP. Recorded April 8 to 18, 2026 in Los Angeles. Produced, mixed and engineered by John Congleton; mastered by Matt Colton. All songs written by Freeman.

Greg Freeman - guitar, vocals; Garrett Linck - bass, group vocals; Joey Sullivan (Florry) - drums, percussion; Carney Hemler (The Rockin Worms) - guitar, group vocals; Sam Atallah - piano, keys, trumpet, horn arrangements, group vocals; Scott Daniel - violin.
Guests: Anna McClellan and Trinity Ace (vocals), David Ralicke (saxophone), Vikram Devasthali (trombone), Mike Bolger (accordion on track 13).

Written while Freeman left his longtime Burlington home and went full-time in music, after jobs as a cemetery landscaper and restaurant line cook (Transgressive). The label name-checks early Pavement and pre-Good News Modest Mouse, with Fugazi and Unwound behind the heavier songs.

Singles: Indu (July 21, with the album announcement), Cahokia (Aug. 26) and Loser's Prize (Sept. 29, the final preview). North American tour starts Oct. 20, with a San Francisco stop at The Independent on Nov. 5.
Lyrics are posted for all 13 tracks. Three have FCC words: 1, 11 and 13.
draft_comment: Sprawling, noisy, horn-flecked indie rock with Americana roots, produced by John Congleton. Record Collector hears Fugazi-style post-hardcore in the heavy parts, and three tracks are FCC, the opener included.

tracks.title: Cahokia
tracks.notes: Opener. Second single (Aug. 26). Vocals by Anna McClellan

tracks.title: Totaled
tracks.notes: Vocals by Anna McClellan. Paste says it grieves a towed Toyota. Record Collector hears 90s alt-rock noise

tracks.title: Culture
tracks.notes: Vocals by Trinity Ace. Paste calls it syncopated, a military march toward doom

tracks.title: Withdrawn
tracks.notes: Vocals by Anna McClellan and Trinity Ace. Saxophone: David Ralicke; trombone: Vikram Devasthali. Paste says it starts sparse and acoustic and ends as a horn-filled anthem

tracks.title: Indu
tracks.notes: Lead single (July 21). Vocals by Anna McClellan. Paste calls it a pop earworm; Record Collector hears psych-y slacker garage

tracks.title: Loser's Prize
tracks.notes: Final single (Sept. 29). Vocals by Anna McClellan. Paste calls it uptempo yet melancholy

tracks.title: Hail Mary
tracks.notes: Vocals by Anna McClellan. Per Paste, the first two minutes are a slow instrumental before the riffs arrive. Record Collector calls it a highlight, Fugazi-style post-hardcore

tracks.title: Decade
tracks.notes: Shortest track. Saxophone: David Ralicke; trombone: Vikram Devasthali. Paste hears Dexys Midnight Runners in the horn bridge

tracks.title: Marooned
tracks.notes: Longest track. Vocals by Trinity Ace. Paste says it opens as a minor-key dirge and builds to a full arrangement. Record Collector calls it pounding, Fugazi-style post-hardcore

tracks.title: Untitled 10
tracks.notes: Saxophone: David Ralicke; trombone: Vikram Devasthali. Per Paste, opens on fuzzed-up guitar and turns into a ballad in the second half. Record Collector calls it a brass-imbued psych wig-out
